scope: Stored Application events from stage125 precise process time window; no new query/start/read.
target_attribution: Both Error1000 message records name cg_se_3000.exe 3.0.0.1988, installed path, PID0x1410/5136 and same creation FILETIME0x1DD69E48403089D; exact creation time matches the stage125 retained process object.
error_record_correlation: Stored descending record metadata followed by the same ordered pipeline filtered to Id1000, displaying the two messages. No sorting or re-query.

wer1001.classification: fact: selected diagnostic fields; association described separately
wer1001.method: Same stored $ev125 filtered to Id1001; XML parsed in guest memory, field names observed, then only EventName and P1..P8 displayed. Index0 then index1, no sorting or re-query.
wer1001.association: Input ordering preserves the stored metadata record order. Same time window and matching app name/version/COFF/status; selected1001 fields do not contain a PID or creation FILETIME. Exact PID/creation binding is from the two1000 records.
limits: StackHash/PCH strings are preserved as opaque report values, not library names, addresses, cause or proof of a mitigation.
No P9/P10 values, report IDs, attached-file paths, StorePath values, dump contents or full XML were displayed/exported.
No stack or additional module mapping obtained.

excluded: No full log export, raw screenshot, account/session identifier, systemwide log scan, crash dump, call stack or live module map.
fault_address_limit: The event labels the value FaultOffset and module unknown; it is not a proved image RVA or absolute VA. See independent layout check.
iso_time_acquisition: Same stored $ev125, filtered to Id1000, TimeCreated.ToString(o); complete two ISO outputs and empty ordinary prompt read back. No re-query.

timeline_derivation.classification: derived, conditional on recorded guest wall-clock chronology and the reviewed script order
timeline_derivation.interpretation: The first Error1000 record creation predates the earliest possible fixed-reader invocation in this run. This is a timestamp/order inference, not an instruction trace.
limits: No reader invocation timestamp was printed.
No loaded module map, faulting instruction or exception stack was captured.
This does not identify the crash cause or establish what influenced the later access violation.
